projectCategory: DSA Module 3.3: Sliding Window & Prefix / Difference Array Mechanics
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K (Fixed Sliding Window)
projects.description: Given an array of integers and a window size K, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of size K. Recomputing subarray sums from scratch takes O(N * K) time. A Fixed Sliding Window updates the sum in O(1) constant time by adding the incoming element `arr[i]` and subtracting the outgoing element `arr[i - K]`. In this project, you will build a Fixed Sliding Window Max Sum Engine in C in O(N) linear time.
projects.learningOutcome: Fixed Sliding Window Pattern, O(1) Window Slide Invariant & O(N) Array Scanning
projects.exampleText: Find max sum subarray of size K=3 in [2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 2]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K ---
Maximum Sum Subarray of Size 3 = 9
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Initial Window**: Compute sum of first K elements.
2. **Slide Window**: `window_sum += arr[i] - arr[i - K]`. Update `max_sum = max(max_sum, window_sum)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_sub_array_of_size_k()`: Computes maximum window sum of size K in O(N) time.

projects.title: First Negative Number in Every Window of Size K
projects.description: Given an array and window size K, print the first negative integer in every contiguous window of size K. Maintain a Queue storing indices of negative numbers within the current window. In this project, you will build a Window First Negative Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Queue-Buffered Sliding Windows, Negative Element Tracking & Boundary Expiration
projects.exampleOutput:
--- First Negative Number in Window K=2 ---
First Negatives: [ -8 0 -6 -6 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Enqueue Negative**: Enqueue index `i` if `arr[i] < 0`.
2. **Prune Queue**: Remove queue front if `queue[front] <= i - K`. Print `arr[queue[front]]` as first negative.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `first_negative_in_window()`: Finds first negative number per window using queue.

projects.title: 1D Prefix Sum Array Construction & O(1) Range Sum Queries
projects.description: Given an array, precompute a Prefix Sum array `P[i] = P[i-1] + arr[i]` in O(N) time. Any subsequent subarray sum query for range `[L .. R]` is answered in instant O(1) time using `Sum[L..R] = P[R] - P[L-1]`. In this project, you will build a 1D Prefix Sum Query Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix Sum Precomputation, Instant O(1) Range Sum Queries & Space-Time Tradeoffs
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 1D Prefix Sum O(1) Range Queries ---
Range Sum [1..3] (20 + 10 + 5) = 35
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Precompute**: `prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + arr[i]`.
2. **Query O(1)**: `prefix[R] - prefix[L-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_prefix_sum()` & `query_range_sum()`: Performs O(1) range sum queries.

projects.title: Difference Array Range Update Engine (arr[L..R] += V in O(1))
projects.description: Applying Q range updates `arr[L..R] += V` directly takes O(N * Q) time. A Difference Array `diff` applies updates in O(1) constant time by modifying boundary points: `diff[L] += V` and `diff[R + 1] -= V`. Running a prefix sum pass reconstructs the final array in O(N + Q) time! In this project, you will build a Difference Array Range Update Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Difference Array Invariants, O(1) Constant Range Updates & Prefix Sum Reconstruction
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Difference Array O(1) Range Updates ---
Reconstructed Array after updates: [ 0 10 10 10 0 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **O(1) Boundary Update**: `diff[L] += V`, `diff[R+1] -= V`.
2. **Prefix Pass**: `arr[i] = arr[i-1] + diff[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_difference_array()` & `reconstruct_array()`: Performs O(1) range updates using difference array.

projects.title: Smallest Subarray with Sum Greater Than or Equal to Target
projects.description: Given an array of positive integers and a target sum, find the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is `>= target`. Use a Dynamic Sliding Window (`left` and `right`). Expand `right` to accumulate sum; contract `left` while `sum >= target` to shrink window length. In this project, you will build a Dynamic Sliding Window Min Subarray Finder in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Sliding Window Expansion/Contraction, Subarray Minimum Bounding & O(N) Processing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Smallest Subarray with Sum >= Target ---
Minimum Subarray Length = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Expand Right**: `sum += nums[right]`.
2. **Contract Left**: While `sum >= target`, update `min_len = min(min_len, right - left + 1)`, subtract `nums[left++]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_subarray_len()`: Finds smallest subarray length with sum >= target.

projects.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
projects.description: Find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters. Maintain a Dynamic Sliding Window `[left .. right]` and a character position map `last[char]`. When encountering a repeated character at index `right`, jump `left = last[char] + 1` to restore uniqueness in O(N) time! In this project, you will build a Unique Substring Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Character Index Map Hashing, Dynamic Window Pointer Jumps & O(N) Substring Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters ---
String: 'abcabcbb' -> Longest Substring Length = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Character Map**: Store last seen index of each character.
2. **Window Jump**: If char seen in current window, set `left = last[char] + 1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `length_of_longest_substring()`: Computes longest unique substring length in O(N) time.

projects.title: Maximum Average Subarray of Size K
projects.description: Find a contiguous subarray of fixed size K that has the maximum average value and return this average. Calculate initial window sum of first K items, then slide window `sum += nums[i] - nums[i - K]`, tracking max average. In this project, you will build a Max Average Subarray Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Floating Point Average Calculation, Fixed Window Accumulation & O(N) Sliding
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Average Subarray of Size K ---
Maximum Average = 12.75000
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sum Window**: Slide fixed window of size K.
2. **Average**: Divide `max_sum` by K.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_max_average()`: Computes maximum average subarray of size K.

projects.title: Find Equilibrium Index of an Array using Prefix Sums
projects.description: An Equilibrium Index is an index such that sum of elements at lower indices equals sum of elements at higher indices (`LeftSum == RightSum`). Compute total sum in pass 1. In pass 2, maintain `left_sum`: `right_sum = total_sum - left_sum - arr[i]`. If `left_sum == right_sum`, return index `i`. In this project, you will build an Equilibrium Index Finder in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Left/Right Prefix Balance, Linear O(N) Pass & Array Partition Analysis
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Array Equilibrium Index Finder ---
Equilibrium Index = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Total Sum**: Calculate `total_sum`.
2. **Balance Check**: Loop `i`: `right_sum = total_sum - left_sum - arr[i]`. Return `i` if `left_sum == right_sum`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `find_equilibrium_index()`: Finds equilibrium index in O(N) time.

projects.title: Product of Array Except Self (Prefix & Suffix Products)
projects.description: Construct an array `ans` such that `ans[i]` equals product of all elements of `nums` except `nums[i]`, WITHOUT using division operator in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space! Build prefix products in `ans` in pass 1; multiply suffix products `R` in pass 2. In this project, you will build Product of Array Except Self in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix/Suffix Product Sweeps, Non-Divisive Multiplication & O(1) Auxiliary Space
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Product of Array Except Self ---
Product Array: [ 24 12 8 6 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Pass**: `ans[i] = prefix_product`.
2. **Suffix Pass**: Multiply `ans[i]` by running suffix product `R`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `product_except_self()`: Calculates product except self using prefix/suffix sweeps.

projects.title: Maximum Consecutive Ones III (Flipping K Zeroes)
projects.description: Given a binary array and integer K, find maximum consecutive 1s in array if you can flip at most K 0s to 1s. Use Dynamic Sliding Window `[left .. right]`. Expand `right`: if `nums[right] == 0`, increment `zero_count++`. If `zero_count > K`, contract `left++` until `zero_count <= K`. In this project, you will build Max Consecutive Ones Finder in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Zero Flips Window Metric, Dynamic Subarray Bounding & Max Length Tracking
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Consecutive Ones III (K Flips) ---
Longest Consecutive Ones Window = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Zero Counter**: Track count of 0s inside window.
2. **Contract Window**: Shrink `left` pointer when 0s count exceeds K.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `longest_ones_k_flips()`: Computes maximum consecutive 1s after K flips.

projects.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
projects.description: Given string S and integer K, find length of longest substring containing same letter after replacing at most K characters. Maintain character frequency table of current window and track `max_freq`. Window is valid if `(window_length - max_freq) <= K`. In this project, you will build a Character Replacement Optimizer in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Frequency Table Window Validation, Replacement Allowance Checks & Substring Optimization
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Repeating Character Replacement ---
Longest Valid Substring Length = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Window Invariant**: `(right - left + 1) - max_freq <= K`.
2. **Slide Left**: If invariant violated, decrement count of `s[left]` and advance `left++`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `character_replacement()`: Solves longest character replacement substring in O(N) time.

projects.title: Minimum Window Substring (Hard Sliding Window Engine)
projects.description: Given strings S and T, find minimum window substring in S that contains all characters of T (including duplicates). Maintain target frequency table for T and current frequency table for window in S. Expand `right` until all chars matched; contract `left` to minimize window length in O(N) time. In this project, you will build a Minimum Window Substring Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Character Matching Windows, Expanding/Contracting Window Invariants & Hard String Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Window Substring ---
Minimum Window Substring of 'ADOBECODEBANC' containing 'ABC' is 'BANC'
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Target**: Count occurrences of chars in T.
2. **Match & Contract**: Expand `right` until all T chars covered. Contract `left` while valid to minimize window size.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_window_demo()`: Solves minimum window substring using sliding window.

projects.title: Subarray Sum Equals K using Prefix Sum Hash Map
projects.description: Find total count of continuous subarrays whose sum equals K. Maintain running `curr_sum` and a Hash Map storing frequencies of prefix sums `map[prefix_sum]`. At each index, add `map[curr_sum - K]` to total count in O(N) linear time! In this project, you will build Subarray Sum K Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix Sum Frequency Hash Maps, Target Difference Lookups & O(N) Subarray Counting
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Subarray Sum Equals K ---
Total Subarrays with Sum 2 = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Sum Map**: Map stores `frequency[prefix_sum]`.
2. **Add Complement Count**: Add `prefix_map[curr_sum - K]` to total count.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `subarray_sum_k()`: Counts subarrays with sum K using prefix sum hash map.

projects.title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
projects.description: Find count of continuous subarrays whose sum is divisible by K. Modulo math rule: if `PrefixSum[i] % K == PrefixSum[j] % K`, the subarray sum between `i+1` and `j` is divisible by K. Handle negative modulo arithmetic properly. In this project, you will build a Divisible Subarray Counter in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Modulo Congruence Invariants, Negative Modulo Normalization & Remainder Hash Maps
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Subarray Sums Divisible by K ---
Total Subarrays Divisible by 5 = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Normalized Modulo**: `rem = (curr_sum % K + K) % K`.
2. **Modulo Hash Map**: Add `mod_map[rem]` to total count, increment `mod_map[rem]++`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `subarrays_div_by_k()`: Counts subarrays divisible by K using modulo remainder maps.

projects.title: 2D Prefix Sum Array Construction & O(1) Submatrix Sum Queries
projects.description: Precompute 2D Prefix Sum grid `P[i][j] = matrix[i-1][j-1] + P[i-1][j] + P[i][j-1] - P[i-1][j-1]` in O(R*C) time. Answer any 2D submatrix sum query `[(r1,c1)..(r2,c2)]` in O(1) time: `P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1]`. In this project, you will build a 2D Submatrix Query Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Grid Prefix Inclusion-Exclusion, Instant O(1) Submatrix Sums & 2D Matrix Precomputation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Prefix Sum O(1) Submatrix Query ---
Submatrix Sum [(1,1)..(2,2)] = 28
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2D Inclusion-Exclusion**: Build `P[i][j]` using top and left region sums.
2. **Query O(1)**: `P[r2+1][c2+1] - P[r1][c2+1] - P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `build_2d_prefix()` & `query_submatrix_sum()`: Performs O(1) 2D submatrix sum queries.

projects.title: 2D Difference Array Matrix Range Updates
projects.description: Apply 2D submatrix updates `matrix[(r1,c1)..(r2,c2)] += V` in O(1) constant time using 2D Difference Array boundary updates: `D[r1][c1] += V`, `D[r1][c2+1] -= V`, `D[r2+1][c1] -= V`, `D[r2+1][c2+1] += V`. Reconstruct final 2D grid using 2D prefix sums. In this project, you will build a 2D Difference Matrix Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Difference Array Math, 4-Corner O(1) Submatrix Updates & 2D Array Defragmentation
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Difference Array Matrix Range Update ---
Applied +5 update to submatrix [(1,1)..(2,2)] in O(1) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **4-Corner Updates**: Modify `(r1,c1)`, `(r1,c2+1)`, `(r2+1,c1)`, and `(r2+1,c2+1)`.
2. **2D Prefix Pass**: Run 2D prefix sum pass to reconstruct updated 2D matrix.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `update_2d_diff()`: Performs O(1) submatrix range updates on 2D difference array.

projects.title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays (K Odd Numbers)
projects.description: A continuous subarray is called Nice if it contains exactly K odd numbers. Reduce to `Exact(K) = AtMost(K) - AtMost(K - 1)` using sliding window odd counters. In this project, you will build a Nice Subarray Counter in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Exact-K Reduction, Sliding Window Odd Counter & O(N) Nice Subarray Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Number of Nice Subarrays (K Odds) ---
Nice Subarrays Count = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Reduction**: `Exact(K) = AtMost(K) - AtMost(K - 1)`.
2. **Sliding Window**: Count subarrays with at most K odd numbers.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `num_subarrays_with_k_odds()`: Counts nice subarrays containing K odd numbers.

projects.title: Fruit Into Baskets (At Most 2 Distinct Elements Window)
projects.description: Given an array representing fruit trees, pick maximum fruits into 2 baskets (meaning sliding window can contain AT MOST 2 distinct fruit types). Expand `right` and shrink `left` when distinct types > 2. In this project, you will build a Fruit Basket Optimizer in C in O(N) time.
projects.learningOutcome: At-Most-2 Distinct Types Constraint, Frequency Table Windowing & Max Fruit Capacity
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fruit Into Baskets (At Most 2 Types) ---
Maximum Harvested Fruits = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Distinct Counter**: Track number of distinct fruit types in window.
2. **Contract Left**: Shrink window when distinct fruit types exceed 2.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `total_fruit()`: Calculates maximum harvested fruits using at-most-2 sliding window.

projects.title: Corporate Flight Bookings / Car Pooling (Difference Array Range Accumulation)
projects.description: Given flight bookings `[first, last, seats]`, calculate total seats reserved for each flight. Use Difference Array: `diff[first] += seats`, `diff[last + 1] -= seats`. Prefix sum pass yields final flight seating allocations in O(N + Q) time. In this project, you will build Flight Booking Difference Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Difference Array Industrial Applications, Reservation Range Updates & O(N+Q) Batch Processing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Corporate Flight Bookings Difference Array ---
Total Seats Allocated per Flight [1..5]: [ 10 55 45 25 25 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Difference Bookings**: `diff[first] += seats`, `diff[last + 1] -= seats`.
2. **Prefix Pass**: Compute running prefix sum for final seat counts.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `corp_flight_bookings_demo()`: Computes total flight bookings using difference array.

projects.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards (Two-Ended Sliding Window)
projects.description: Given card values and integer K, take exactly K cards from either the beginning or end of row to maximize total score. Equivalent to finding minimum sum subarray of size `N - K`! Alternatively, slide window of K cards starting from taking K from left to taking K from right. In this project, you will build a Card Score Maximizer in C in O(K) time.
projects.learningOutcome: Two-Ended Card Selection, Inverse Window Minimization & O(K) Score Optimization
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Points from Cards ---
Maximum Card Score = 12
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Initial K Left**: Compute sum of first K cards.
2. **Slide Right**: Replace card `K - 1 - i` from left with card `N - 1 - i` from right, updating max score.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_score()`: Calculates maximum card score using two-ended sliding window.

projects.title: Sliding Window Maximum using Monotonic Deque
projects.description: Find maximum element in every sliding window of size K as it moves across array of size N in linear O(N) time. Standard sorting takes O(N * K). Maintain a Monotonic Decreasing Deque storing indices of potential maximums. In this project, you will build a Monotonic Deque Window Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotonic Decreasing Deque, Linear O(N) Sliding Window Maximum & Out-of-Window Pruning
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sliding Window Maximum Monotonic Deque ---
Window Maxima: [ 3 3 5 5 6 7 ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Monotonic Deque**: Maintain indices in decreasing order of array values.
2. **Window Max**: `arr[deque[front]]` is maximum for current window.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_sliding_window()`: Computes sliding window maximums in O(N) time.

projects.title: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
projects.description: Given binary array `nums` and integer K, flip K consecutive bits at a time to make all elements 1. Return minimum number of K-bit flips required. Maintain a sliding difference array/flag `is_flipped` tracking cumulative flips affecting current position in O(N) time and O(1) space! In this project, you will build K-Bit Flip Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Greedy Bit Flipping, Cumulative Flip State Tracking & Linear O(N) Bit Array Processing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum K Consecutive Bit Flips ---
Minimum Flips Required = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cumulative Flip State**: Maintain `is_flipped` flag using sliding window history.
2. **Greedy Flip**: If current bit needs flipping (`nums[i] == is_flipped`), flip window `[i .. i+K-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_k_bit_flips()`: Calculates minimum K-bit flips in linear O(N) time.

projects.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K (Monotonic Queue + Prefix Sums)
projects.description: Find shortest non-empty subarray with sum `>= K` in an array containing POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE numbers. Standard sliding window fails due to negative numbers breaking monotonicity. Use Prefix Sums `P[i]` and a Monotonic Increasing Deque of prefix sum indices in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Shortest Subarray Sum K Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Prefix Sum Monotonic Deque, Handling Negative Array Values & O(N) Shortest Subarray Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Subarray Sum at Least K ---
Shortest Subarray Length = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prefix Sums**: Compute `P[i]` array.
2. **Monotonic Deque**: Maintain `P[i]` in increasing order in deque. Contract `front` when `P[i] - P[deque[front]] >= K`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `shortest_subarray_sum_at_least_k()`: Solves shortest subarray sum >= K with negative numbers in O(N) time.

projects.title: Dynamic 2D Range Addition & Prefix Sum Matrix Queries
projects.description: Perform dynamic 2D submatrix range updates and answer submatrix sum queries efficiently. Combines 2D Difference Array updates with 2D Prefix Sum precomputation. In this project, you will build a Dynamic 2D Matrix Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Composite 2D Grid Structures, Dynamic 2D Difference Updates & Submatrix Sums
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic 2D Range Addition & Prefix Sum Matrix ---
Applied O(1) 2D range update and built 2D prefix sum grid in O(R*C).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Difference Updates**: Apply 4-corner updates for submatrix additions.
2. **Prefix Grid**: Reconstruct 2D prefix sum array to answer submatrix queries in O(1).
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dynamic_2d_range_demo()`: Demonstrates dynamic 2D range updates and prefix sum queries.

projects.title: Multi-Threaded SIMD Accelerated Sliding Window Kernel
projects.description: High-throughput audio and digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms compute sliding window averages/filters across gigabyte streams. Use SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) 256-bit AVX2 vector instructions and multi-threading to process 8 window positions per CPU clock cycle. In this project, you will build SIMD Sliding Window Simulator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 Vectorization, Hardware-Parallel Window Processing & DSP Sliding Kernels
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Multi-Threaded SIMD Accelerated Sliding Window Kernel ---
Executed 256-bit AVX2 vector sliding window sum in hardware parallel passes.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Vector Register**: Load 8 float/int values into 256-bit AVX2 register.
2. **Hardware Parallel Add**: Perform SIMD vector sliding window sums in 1 clock cycle.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_sliding_window_demo()`: Simulates SIMD vectorized sliding window kernel.
